questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: Match the oral drug class to the mechanism or note in the page columns — 1) Biguanide 2) Sulfonylurea 3) Oral GLP-1 analogue 4) SGLT-2 antagonist … A) Metformin/AMP kinase B) Gliclazide with K+ channel action in the column C) Semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide D) Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin
questions.exp: The four page columns are biguanide/metformin, sulfonylurea/gliclazide, oral GLP-1 analogues and SGLT-2 antagonists with the listed examples. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: The metformin column says it acts by increasing ___ kinase.
questions.exp: Metformin is annotated as acting by increased AMP kinase. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: What HbA1c-reduction range is written in the metformin column?
questions.exp: The metformin column gives good HbA1c reduction of 1–2%. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: Assess the metformin notes: I There is no hypoglycemia risk in the column. II The cardiac line points to no risk.
questions.exp: The metformin column says no hypoglycemia risk and shows the cardiac line leading to no risk. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: A patient has the renal function threshold written in the metformin column. Which page instruction applies?
opts: Metformin is used only when GFR is exactly 30 mL/min
Metformin is contraindicated when GFR is below 30 mL/min
Metformin is increased when GFR is below 30 mL/min
Metformin is replaced by insulin at GFR above 90 mL/min
questions.exp: The metformin column lists contraindication at GFR <30 mL/min. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: Match the drug column to its distinctive page note — 1) Metformin 2) Gliclazide 3) Oral GLP-1 analogue 4) SGLT-2 antagonist … A) Combats resistance B) Only drug in use, antioxidant and vasodilator C) Used in NASH and protective glycemic/cardio/renal notes D) Blocks NLRP3 inflammasome pathway
questions.exp: Those distinctive notes appear in the respective four oral-drug columns. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: What HbA1c-reduction range is written for the oral GLP-1 analogue column?
questions.exp: The oral GLP-1 analogue column states HbA1c reduction of 2–5%. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: Assess the SGLT-2 notes: I Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are named. II The column says blockade of the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway blocks atherosclerosis.
questions.exp: The SGLT-2 column names dapagliflozin and empagliflozin and draws NLRP3 inflammasome-pathway blockade toward blocked atherosclerosis. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: Which group is listed under indications of insulin therapy?
opts: Only a normal glucose value before meals
Hybrid diabetes form, T1DM, GDM, HbA1c ≥9.5%, vascular involvement, ketosis or significant polyuria/polydipsia with weight loss
Only mild weight gain with HbA1c below 5.7%
questions.exp: The insulin-indications list includes hybrid form, T1DM, GDM, HbA1c ≥9.5%, macro/microvascular involvement, ketosis and significant polyuria/polydipsia with weight loss. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: Match the insulin type to its page example — 1) Ultra short 2) Short 3) Intermediate 4) Long/ultralong … A) Lispro and Aspart B) Regular C) NPH D) Glargine, Detemir / Degludec
questions.exp: The insulin-type line gives ultra-short lispro/aspart, short regular, intermediate NPH, long glargine/detemir and ultralong degludec. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the names printed in the oral GLP-1 analogue column?
questions.exp: Semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide are in the oral GLP-1 analogue column; gliclazide is in the sulfonylurea column. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 oral hypoglycemic drugs and insulin
questions.q: The final line on this page says CGM should be done before starting:
questions.exp: The CGM line states that continuous blood glucose monitoring should be done before starting insulin therapy. (Book p933)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: The treatment written below the dawn-phenomenon graph is:
questions.exp: The dawn-phenomenon note gives increase night-time insulin dose. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: Match the graph pattern to the page label — 1) Early-morning hyperglycemia without the 3 a.m. low 2) 3 a.m. hypoglycemia followed by morning hyperglycemia 3) Excess night insulin 4) Somogyi treatment … A) Dawn phenomenon B) Somogyi effect C) Midnight hypoglycemia D) Decrease night-time insulin dose
questions.exp: The page labels the first graph dawn phenomenon, the second Somogyi effect, links excess night insulin to midnight hypoglycemia, and gives a decreased night dose as treatment. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: Assess the Somogyi notes: I Counter-regulatory hormones are linked to early-morning hyperglycemia. II Excess nighttime insulin is linked to midnight hypoglycemia.
questions.exp: Both arrows are written under the Somogyi graph. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: A glucose tracing shows hypoglycemia at 3 a.m. followed by early-morning hyperglycemia. Which page label fits?
questions.exp: The Somogyi graph explicitly marks hypoglycemia at 3.00 am followed by fasting hyperglycemia. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: Which regular-insulin schedule is written under insulin regime?
questions.exp: The insulin-regime line gives regular insulin 8–8–8. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: Match the basal insulin option to the exact schedule — 1) Glargine 2) Degludec 3) Regular insulin basal option … A) 16 U at 11 PM daily B) 16 U on alternate night C) 16 U twice daily
questions.exp: The page lists glargine 16 U at night daily, degludec 16 U on alternate nights and regular 16 U BD daily. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: After insulin, base glucose is to be assessed how many times?
questions.exp: The page says base glucose levels should be accessed 6 times. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: The six base-glucose checks are pre- and post- breakfast, lunch and ___.
questions.exp: The list specifies pre- and post-breakfast, pre- and post-lunch, and pre- and post-dinner. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: Assess the dose-adjustment rule: I A dose may be increased by 2 units. II A dose may be decreased by 4 units.
questions.exp: The final insulin-regime bullet gives increase by 2 units or decrease by 4 units. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: Which item is labelled a component of the continuous glucose monitoring system?
questions.exp: The CGMS diagram labels continuous glucose monitor, cable, glucose sensor and com-station; glucose sensor is one component. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: Match the CGMS equipment label to its page description — 1) Sensor 2) Charger/com-station 3) Recorder 4) Inserter … A) Skin sensor B) Charging/display unit C) Recording device D) Insertion device
questions.exp: The equipment drawings are labelled sensor, charger/com-station, recorder and inserter. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the two named overnight glucose patterns?
questions.exp: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and fasting hyperglycemia appear in the overnight tracing notes; postprandial hypoglycemia does not. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Match the macro-priority to the page's comorbidity marker — 1) Heart 2) Kidney 3) Glycemic/weight line 4) Better-outcome addition … A) HF/ASCVD B) Albuminuria C) HbA1c and weight to metformin D) SGLT-2 inhibitor ± GLP-1 analogue
questions.exp: The treatment flow marks HbA1c/weight leading to metformin, heart HF/ASCVD and kidney albuminuria as macro priorities, and SGLT-2 inhibitor ± GLP-1 analogue for better outcome; the lower flow also labels a reserved drug as DPP-4 inhibitors and Gliclazide. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Assess the SGLT-2 counselling list: I Euglycemic ketoacidosis is listed. II Mycotic and genital infection are listed.
questions.exp: The SGLT-2 side-effect advice lists euglycemic ketoacidosis, mycotic infection and genital infection. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Which blood-pressure targets are written under comorbidity-driven treatment?
opts: Below 130/80 without kidney disease and below 120/80 with kidney disease
Below 120/80 without kidney disease and below 130/80 with kidney disease
questions.exp: The page gives <130/80 without kidney disease and <120/80 with kidney disease. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: What LDL target is written for a diabetic patient over 40 years with cardiovascular, peripheral vascular or heart disease?
questions.exp: The LDL target branch for CVD/PVD/heart disease is <55 mg/dL. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Match the LDL-risk branch to the printed target — 1) Normally 2) Diabetic over 40 without risk factors 3) Diabetic over 40 with one risk factor 4) CVD/PVD/heart disease … A) <130 mg/dL B) <100 mg/dL C) <70 mg/dL D) <55 mg/dL
questions.exp: The LDL flowchart gives normally <130, no risk factors <100, one risk factor <70, and CVD/PVD/heart disease <55 mg/dL. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Which statin doses are written below the LDL target flowchart?
questions.exp: The treatment line states rosuvastatin 20 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: What aspirin dose is written for a diabetic patient over 40 years with one risk factor?
questions.exp: The aspirin line says add 75 mg aspirin for the listed over-40 diabetic patient with one risk factor. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: A patient with the page's NASH label is being managed. Which investigation and treatment pair is written?
opts: ECG recommended; metformin and insulin listed
ERCP recommended; tacrolimus and aspirin listed
Bone scan recommended; gliclazide and degludec listed
Fibroscan recommended; semaglutide and saroglitazar listed
questions.exp: The NASH line recommends Fibroscan and lists semaglutide and saroglitazar. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Saroglitazar is labelled a dual PPAR-___ + γ agonist.
questions.exp: The NASH treatment line calls saroglitazar a dual PPAR-α + γ agonist. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Assess the proteinuria rule: I ACE inhibitor, SGLT-2 inhibitor and finerenone are listed. II Finerenone is labelled a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist.
questions.exp: The proteinuria line lists ACE inhibitor, SGLT-2 inhibitor and finerenone, identifying finerenone as a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Match the over-40 diabetic risk factor to the exact examples — 1) First 2) Second 3) Third 4) Fourth … A) Hypertension B) Dyslipidemia C) Swelling D) Family history of CKD
questions.exp: The risk-factor line lists hypertension, dyslipidemia, swelling and family history of CKD before the 75-mg aspirin instruction. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Diabetic treatment and comorbidity-driven management
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the treatments named for proteinuria?
questions.exp: ACE inhibitor, SGLT-2 inhibitor and finerenone are listed for proteinuria; semaglutide appears in the NASH line. (Book p935)
